extraction.name: SeamlessAlign
extraction.description: SeamlessAlign is the largest open dataset for multimodal translation to date, totaling 470,000 hours of automatically aligned speech translations. It was created using parallel data mining with SONAR multilingual and multimodal sentence embeddings. The dataset covers 37 languages and includes: English speech to non-English text (approximately 200,000 hours), Non-English speech to English text (approximately 240,000 hours), and Non-English speech to English speech (approximately 29,000 hours). The dataset was built as part of the SeamlessM4T project to support massively multilingual and multimodal machine translation.
extraction.creator: Meta AI (Seamless Communication team), INRIA, UC Berkeley
extraction.inLanguage: 37 languages including Arabic, Bengali, Catalan, Czech, Mandarin Chinese, Welsh, Danish, German, Estonian, Finnish, French, Hindi, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Kannada, Korean, Maltese, Dutch, Persian, Polish, Portuguese, Romanian, Russian, Slovak, Spanish, Swedish, Swahili, Tamil, Telugu, Tagalog, Thai, Turkish, Ukrainian, Urdu, Uzbek, Vietnamese
extraction.citeAs: Seamless Communication et al., SeamlessM4T: Massively Multilingual & Multimodal Machine Translation, arXiv:2308.11596, 2023
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Parallel data mining approach: starting with a large collection of raw audio (4 million hours from publicly available repository of crawled web data), audio files were chunked into overlapping segments and speech Language Identification (LID) was applied. Speech and text corpora were projected into a common embedding space (SONAR), in which mining was performed to identify translation pairs with optimal segmentation. On the text side, the same sentence-segmented dataset from NLLB was used.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw audio originates from a publicly available repository of crawled web data (4 million hours total, approximately 1 million hours in English). Text data is drawn from the NLLB dataset. Speech encoders trained on human-provided ASR transcripts.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Audio pre-processing included: deduplicating audio file URLs, downloading audio files, resampling at 16KHz, filtering out non-speech data with a bespoke audio event detection (AED) model. Audio segmentation using Voice Activity Detection (VAD) followed by over-segmentation strategy creating overlapping splits. Text data cleaning and filtering followed NLLB pipeline run at scale with Stopes library.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Speech Language Identification (LID) was applied to audio segments with filtering based on per-language Gaussian distribution thresholds (rejecting 8% of data). Over-segmentation approach used to create multiple possible overlapping splits. Embeddings computed with SONAR encoders, indexed with FAISS library. Mining performed using margin criterion with threshold of 1.15 on margin score. Length filtering removed pairs where utterance is shorter than 0.1s or longer than 50s, or text longer than 250 sub-words. Toxicity imbalance filter applied with threshold of 1.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Alignment is automatic using cosine similarity and margin-based scoring in SONAR joint embedding space. For human evaluation of outputs (separate from SeamlessAlign creation), XSTS protocol was used with 3-5 annotators per item, median score taken, calibration set methodology applied. MOS protocol used for naturalness evaluation with Likert scale (1-5).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For XSTS human evaluation: when 3 annotators had a disagreement of score values of 2 or more, 2 additional annotators evaluated the same item again (totaling 5 evaluator scores). Median score over annotators taken for robustness. Cross-lingual calibration set used with 'moderated calibration' methodology to reduce language-level annotator biases.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 annotators per item (up to 5 when disagreement of 2+ points occurred) for XSTS; 3 annotators for most MOS languages, 1 for some languages
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: SONAR text and speech encoders, FAISS library for similarity search, Stopes library for mining pipeline, w2v-BERT 2.0 for speech representation, ECAPA-TDNN based LID model (LID100), Silero Voice Activity Detection (VAD), Audio Event Detection (AED) model, Whisper (for ASR-BLEU evaluation), NLLB-200-3.3B (for pseudo-labeling)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Open-sourced metadata to recreate the unfiltered 470,000 hours of SeamlessAlign available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/seamless_communication. Mining code open-sourced in the Stopes library. Optimal threshold can be tuned based on task.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Training data was mined from publicly available web sources. Although the authors invested heavily in data cleaning, personally identifiable information may not be entirely eliminated. Languages covered include low-resource languages spanning various geographies and cultures.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The work aims to augment 'world-readiness' by streamlining multilingual exchange across contexts. Benefits include improved accessibility for individuals who are blind or visually impaired (295+ million people globally), those with literacy limitations (773 million adults), and speakers of languages with script variance. Risks include making groups with lower digital literacy more vulnerable to misinformation or online scams if misappropriated by bad actors. Authors note translations should augment rather than replace language learning or reliable human interpreters, especially in high-stakes legal/medical contexts.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Gender bias evaluation on Multilingual HolisticBias showed SeamlessM4T overgeneralizes to masculine forms when translating from neutral terms (average preference of ~10%), and shows lack of robustness when varying gender by ~3%. Gender representation analysis reveals overrepresentation of masculine lexica compared to feminine in analyzed training datasets. Performance varies by resource level with low-resource languages typically performing worse. ASR performance may vary based on gender, race, accent, or language.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Dataset is limited to 37 languages (not full 100 language coverage). Word list-based toxicity detection has limitations around tokenization and context-dependent toxicity. Gender bias measured through linguistic gender clues as proxy may not generalize. Model is not intended for production deployment, domain-specific inputs (medical/legal), long-form translation, or certified translations. Performance varies across user demographics. Direct S2ST models may suffer from truncations/omissions in longer audio durations.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Primary use cases: Training multimodal and multilingual translation models supporting ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition for 96 languages), S2ST (Speech-to-Speech translation), S2TT (Speech-to-Text translation), T2ST (Text-to-Speech translation), T2TT (Text-to-Text translation), and TTS (Text-to-Speech synthesis). Primary intended users are researchers and the machine translation research community. Used as training data combined with human-labeled and pseudo-labeled data totaling 406,000 hours.
